title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is not a manuscript page. It is a typed page, printed upside down in the scan, from SGA 7 I, Exposé IX (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), page IX-51, opening §5. It was evidently reused as scrap paper: faint handwritten De Rham/divided-power notes from cote 136 show through from the back. Archive stamp 369, marginal number 802.

The setting is as follows. V is a henselian discrete valuation ring, S = Spec V, A is an abelian variety over the generic point and A^o is the identity component of its Néron model. In case 2.2.3, A^o is ℓ-divisible. The fixed part T_ℓ(A^o)^f ⊂ T_ℓ(A) is then the Barsotti–Tate pro-ℓ-group formed by the finite parts (_{ℓ^ν}A^o)^f.

Section 5 aims to extend the orthogonality theorem (the toric part as orthogonal of the fixed part under the Weil pairing) to the case ℓ = p in the semi-stable situation. To do so, it redefines the toric part of T_ℓ(A^o) without assuming ℓ ≠ p, but assuming S complete. The construction runs in three steps:
- Let S_n = Spec(V/m^{n+1}) and X_n = X ×_S S_n.
- (A^o)_n is smooth over S_n. By the rigidity and lifting of tori (SGA 3 IX 3.6 bis), the maximal torus T_o of the special fibre lifts uniquely to a subtorus T_n ⊂ A^o_n.
- By uniqueness, the T_n are compatible under base change S_{n'} → S_n. They therefore form a formal subtorus T̂ of the formal completion Â^o along the special fibre.

According to its footnote, completeness is removed later, in §6.1. In SGA 7 the p-divisible group of T̂ then serves as the toric part for ℓ = p, which feeds the later results on duality of B_o and B'_o and on criteria for good and semi-stable reduction.

ideas.what: Unique lifting of the maximal torus of the special fibre to infinitesimal neighbourhoods, giving a formal subtorus of the completed Néron model
ideas.modern_name: Formal torus / toric part of the Néron model; rigidity of tori
ideas.where_published: SGA 7 I, Exp. IX, §5.1 (this very page); SGA 3 Exp. IX 3.6 bis

ideas.what: Orthogonality theorem (fixed part vs toric part) extended to ℓ = p in the semi-stable case
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck's orthogonality theorem / semi-stable reduction theory

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typed page of the published SGA 7 I Exposé IX, reused as scrap paper, so its content is fully published and credited. The only archival point of interest is the reuse of SGA 7 typescript for the 1975–76 divided-power De Rham notes.
transcription_corrections: The image is upside down. The page is a typed SGA 7 I Exp. IX p. 51 typescript, not a handwritten note, and should be catalogued as such.
The faint show-through handwriting belongs to the manuscript notes on the reverse side and is not transcribed.
The handwritten '369' is a faint mirror-image show-through from the back, not marginal text on this side.
